Title: Careleaves: Japan's Bandage With a Secretly Genius Name

Description:
Found this Careleaves bandage on the shelf at Don Quijote in Osaka, and its name isn't random at all. Careleaves comes from CARE + LEAF (the bandage is even shaped like a leaf), and it echoes the English word "leave" too, as in wishing your wound goodbye. It launched in 1997 after three years of development, switching to a high-density urethane nonwoven fabric that stretches both ways so it flexes when you bend a finger. Reviews are split: plenty say it stays put even when bent, but some warn against wearing it too long on delicate skin.
